_note: Core motion vocabulary (brand-free). A technique is a motion format: its layouts, the classes it allows and its defaults. A brand may keep to some techniques (motion.techniques in its profile) and adds its motifs (motion.motifs). Every phrase here becomes direction Claude Motion follows.
_hold: How long every scene holds after its last entrance lands, still moving, before anything leaves: a second for every `read` characters on screen, at least `min` and at most `max` seconds (Ian, Oct 12: 3 s; then a spacer that grows with the scene's text). `read:` in the front matter or hold= on a scene changes it.

story.safe: keep words and the logo clear of the top 250 px, the bottom 420 px and the right 120 px, where the apps draw over the film

post.safe: keep words and the logo at least 80 px from every edge

square.safe: keep words and the logo at least 80 px from every edge

wide.safe: keep words and the logo at least 96 px from every edge

energy._note: half: seconds of each transition half; stagger: seconds between pieces; overshoot: the back-out on arrivals.

calm.say: Calm: long eased moves, small overshoots, slow drifts

lively.say: Lively: brisk eased moves with a clear overshoot and settle, every hold still alive

bold.say: Bold: fast snappy moves, big overshoots, strong contrast between scenes

grounds._note: What a scene stands on, from the brand's roles. Ink and colors on it are picked by contrast.

main.say: the brand's main color, full bleed

backdrops._note: A moving layer between the ground and the words, in the scene's colors, always quieter than the words.
backdrops.shapes: two or three large flat shapes (a circle, a rounded square, a quarter circle) bleeding off the edges in the scene's second and third colors, drifting and turning slowly; never under a line of words at full strength
backdrops.rings: concentric rings in the scene's second color, centered off-frame, slowly expanding outward one after another
backdrops.dots: a fine dot grid in a quiet mix of the ink, moving slowly upward with a little parallax; a few dots light up in the second color
backdrops.grid: thin grid lines in a quiet mix of the ink, the camera gliding slowly across them
backdrops.glow: one or two large soft light pools in the scene's second color, slowly wandering behind the words
backdrops.stripes: broad diagonal bands in the scene's second and third colors, sliding slowly along their length
backdrops.ribbons: two long flowing curved ribbons in the scene's second and third colors, gently undulating across the frame
backdrops.bars: tall bars of varying height in quiet mixes of the scene's colors along the bottom edge, rising and falling slowly like a level meter
backdrops.motif: the brand's motif (below), drawn on, then swaying gently in place: its centre stays where it was drawn, roughly the middle of the frame across, and never travels off; follow its own rules

transitions._note: How a scene arrives (`in=` on the scene). Each is two halves: the end of the previous scene and the start of this one meet on the same frame, so the cut can't be seen. {panel} is a brand color chosen apart from both grounds; {next} the arriving scene's ground; {half} the seconds of each half.

cut.in: nothing: a deliberate hard cut, content already arriving

fade.out: over its last {half} s a full-frame layer in the next scene's ground ({next}) fades in over everything
fade.in: it opens on its bare ground, content arriving after {in} s

wipe.out: over its last {half} s a full-frame panel in {panel} sweeps in from the {from} edge (eased in) until it covers the frame
wipe.in: it opens fully covered by that {panel} panel, which leaves toward the {to} edge over the first {half} s (eased out), revealing the scene

slide.out: over its last {half} s its whole stage slides out toward the {to} edge while the next scene's bare ground ({next}) slides in behind it from the {from} edge, so the last frame is that ground alone
slide.in: it opens on its bare ground, content arriving from the {from} side after {in} s

iris.out: over its last {half} s a circle in {panel} grows from the center of its main object until it covers the frame
iris.in: it opens covered in {panel}; a circle opens from the center over the first {half} s, revealing the scene

blinds.out: over its last {half} s six vertical bands in {panel} close in turn, left to right, until they cover the frame
blinds.in: it opens covered by those six {panel} bands, which open in turn, left to right, over the first {half} s

zoom.out: over its last {half} s the camera pushes in fast (to about 160 %) while a full-frame layer in the next scene's ground ({next}) fades in
zoom.in: it opens on its bare ground, content scaling down from about 115 % as it arrives after {in} s

morph.out: over its last {half} s its main object (what moved last) grows and changes shape until it fills the frame in the next scene's ground ({next})
morph.in: it opens on its bare ground, the frame the last scene ended on

chrome.out: over its last {half} s, with the camera already back out at the whole screen, the page content (everything but the shared chrome: header, navigation, sidebar) fades and lifts about 24 px away, leaving the chrome alone on an empty page
chrome.in: it opens on exactly the same chrome, pixel for pixel, over an empty page; its own page content rises in over the first {half} s, staggered top to bottom

zoom-through.out: over its last {half} s the camera pushes through its main object (to about 400 %), eased in, while the next scene's ground ({next}) rises behind it until it alone fills the frame
zoom-through.in: it opens on its bare ground, the camera settling from about 115 % to 100 % over the first {half} s as its content starts to arrive

reframe.out: over its last {half} s the camera pulls back until the whole {screen_from} screen shows as a window on the ground ({next}), its content fades to the window's empty page, and the window starts to change shape toward the {screen_to} screen's proportions
reframe.in: it opens on that empty window, halfway between the two shapes; over the first {half} s the window finishes changing into the {screen_to} screen's proportions and grows to its place on the stage while the new layout builds inside it

roles._note: What a block is. size: its default size class; type: the brand type role it is set in.

eyebrow.say: the eyebrow, in the scene's main color

note.say: the small note, quiet but legible

stat.say: the big number, in the scene's main color

cta.say: the call to action, on a pill in the scene's main color

screen.say: the screenshot the UI is rebuilt from

classes._note: Fixed vocabulary. kind: size, enter, emphasis (the accent word), hold, exit, action (what happens in a walkthrough's UI, one per block, in order); one of each per block. Placeholders: {from} {stagger} {overshoot} {text} {field} {zoom} {cps} {toast}.

rise.say: rises about 40 px into place as it fades in, with a small overshoot

slide.say: slides in from the left edge of the frame, easing out

words.say: enters word by word from the right ({stagger} s apart)

mask.say: rises line by line from behind an invisible edge (each line clipped at its own baseline), {stagger} s apart

type.say: types out letter by letter, about 24 a second, with a caret

split.say: assembles letter by letter, each letter flying in from a small random offset and rotation to its place

zoom.say: scales down from about 140 % to its size as it fades in

blur.say: comes into focus from a soft blur as it fades in

flip.say: flips in around its horizontal axis like a card turning over

count.say: counts from {from} to its value in whole steps, no faster than three changes a second, and lands with a settle

pop.say: pops in from a dot with an overshoot of about {overshoot}

grow.say: grows from a dot to full size with a gentle settle

stamp.say: lands from large (about 180 %) like a stamp, with a short squash on impact

bounce.say: drops in from above the frame and bounces twice before it settles

wipe.say: is revealed by a wipe from left to right

drop.say: drops into place from above and settles

build.say: builds piece by piece, {stagger} s apart

draw.say: draws itself on as a line, then fills

highlight.say: after it lands, a marker band in the scene's second color sweeps behind the accent word

underline.say: after it lands, a hand-drawn underline in the scene's second color draws on under the accent word

circle.say: after it lands, a hand-drawn loop in the scene's second color circles the accent word

drift.say: while held, drifts about 3 px a second

breathe.say: while held, breathes in scale by about 2 % on a 3 s cycle

float.say: while held, floats up and down a few px on a slow cycle

pan.say: while held, pushes in slowly (3 % over the hold)

wobble.say: while held, sways a degree either way on a slow cycle

pulse.say: while held, pulses gently once a second (2 % scale)

out.say: leaves the way it came, reversed and quicker

stay.say: stays until the cut and rides the transition out

click.say: the cursor travels to the control labelled "{text}" (about 1 s, eased, along a gentle curve), settles on it for 0.4 s, then clicks: the control presses in and a ripple spreads from the cursor

fill.say: the cursor clicks into the field labelled "{field}", which shows its focus ring; then "{text}" types into it one letter at a time at an even {cps} letters a second, the caret solid while it types and blinking once it stops

choose.say: the cursor clicks the "{field}" menu, which opens with a short drop; it settles on "{text}", which highlights, and clicks it; the menu closes with the choice in place

focus.say: the camera pushes in on "{text}" (about {zoom}×) over about 1 s, eased, keeping the frame inside the UI

back.say: the camera pulls back out to the whole screen over about 1 s, eased

scroll.say: the page scrolls smoothly (eased, about 1 s) until "{text}" is in view

open.say: the panel or dialog "{text}" scales in from the control that opened it, with a small overshoot; everything behind it dims under a soft scrim (about 50 %) and a light blur, so it is the only subject

close.say: the panel or dialog "{text}" scales back toward where it came from and the page behind comes back into focus

wait.say: "{text}" shows a small spinner that turns into a check after about 1 s

toast.say: a toast reading "{text}" slides in at the {toast} with a small overshoot, holds, and slides away before the scene ends

show.say: "{text}" appears in the UI the way the UI would show it: a row, card or badge rising in with a slight overshoot (rows and cards staggered)

lists.plain: a stacked list, one line per item
lists.chips: rounded pills in the scene's second color (ink chosen for contrast), wrapping onto lines
lists.cards: cards on a quiet panel of the ground, one per item, each with its icon when it has one
lists.steps: a vertical timeline: a line draws down and each item lands on a numbered dot
lists.checks: each item gets a check mark that draws on as the item lands

frames.none: the picture as it is, cropped to its slot
frames.card: on a rounded card with a soft shadow
frames.arch: cropped to an arch (a rectangle with a round top)
frames.browser: inside a simple light browser window
frames.phone: inside Prism's phone mockup (a screenshot on its screen)
frames.tablet: inside Prism's tablet mockup (a screenshot on its screen)
frames.laptop: inside Prism's laptop mockup (a screenshot on its screen)

music.calm: a calm, warm wordless score: a soft pad and an electric piano, a light pulse, rising into the end card; a soft whoosh on each transition
music.bright: a bright, mid-tempo wordless score: marimba and a light kit, building into the end card; a whoosh on each transition

stat-story.name: Stat story
stat-story.look: Number-led brand data story: big numbers that count, charts that build, bold brand-colored grounds that change scene to scene, moving backdrops, every element arriving and leaving with intent

title.say: Opening card: the title is already readable at frame 0 (the thumbnail).

stat.say: One number carries the scene; it arrives first and everything else follows it.

chart.say: A chart builds in order of the data; the highlighted values land last.

compare.say: Before and after side by side or stacked; the change is what moves.

list.say: A short list, one item at a time.

quote.say: A quote, set large, with its attribution.

closing.say: End card: held at least 3 s, the logo lands on the score's last hit, nothing leaves and nothing moves after it settles but the backdrop.

rules: One number per stat scene; the number is the biggest thing on screen.
Counts and charts reach their real values from the format file, never rounded or changed.
Every scene has its own ground and backdrop as given; neighbouring scenes never look alike.

kinetic.name: Kinetic type
kinetic.look: Type-led brand film: one idea per scene, lines that mask up, split and stamp in, grounds that flip between the brand's colors, the accent word landing hard and staying

title.say: Opening card: the title is already readable at frame 0 (the thumbnail).

statement.say: One statement fills the frame; words move, nothing else competes.

list.say: A short list, one item at a time, each replacing or stacking on the last.

quote.say: A quote, set large, with its attribution.

closing.say: End card: held at least 3 s, the logo lands on the score's last hit, nothing leaves and nothing moves after it settles but the backdrop.

rules: Words enter from the same side across the whole film unless a class says otherwise.
Emphasis is motion and the accent word's color or mark, never bold or exclamation marks.
Every scene has its own ground and backdrop as given; neighbouring scenes never look alike.

walkthrough.name: UI walkthrough
walkthrough.look: Product walkthrough: the real app rebuilt full-screen from its screenshots, a calm camera that pushes in on each action and pulls back out, a cursor that settles before it clicks, a step card in the corner that collapses to a chip, and everything that isn't the subject blurred back

title.say: Opening screen: the logo or product name animates in and holds (readable at frame 0, the thumbnail), then the camera zooms through into the app. It never persists into the next scene.

app.say: Meet the app: the UI builds in (header, then navigation, then content, staggered) with the whole screen in view, then the camera pushes in slowly. Never opens already zoomed in with content cut off at an edge.

step.say: One numbered step, one continuous scene: one feature, one task. The step card opens first; the actions follow once it has collapsed.

closing.say: End card: the whole UI has faded out; the logo, one short line, a recap of the steps and the call to action, held at least 4 s; nothing leaves and nothing moves after it settles but the backdrop.

rules: The step card sits bottom-left (above the safe band on tall stages): the step number in a disc, a small eyebrow ("Step 2 of 5"), the title, one sentence and progress dots. About 2 s after its text lands it collapses to a chip (number and title only) to free the screen; it opens again to introduce the next step.
Typing finishes before the click that sends it.
Before the end card the whole UI fades out; the end card recaps the steps by their titles.

screens._note: The device a walkthrough's UI is built for (screen= on a scene). ratio: width / height. The stage decides how it sits: full (fills the frame edge to edge), crop (fills the stage's height; the camera pans across it and never shows past its edges) or device (in core's device mockup, full height, centred).

desktop.say: the desktop layout, built at 1440 px wide

tablet.say: the tablet layout, built at 834 px wide, portrait

phone.say: the phone layout, built at 390 px wide

fits.full: the UI fills the whole frame, edge to edge: never a small window on a background
fits.crop: the UI fills the stage's height and is wider than the stage: the camera frames the part where the action is and pans with it, eased, never showing past the UI's edges
fits.device: the UI sits in core's {device} mockup, as tall as the stage allows inside the safe area, centred; the camera pushes in on the device for each action

walkthrough._note: The house rules every walkthrough film follows (Ian, Oct 13: the UI walkthrough video UX rules). Numbers here are what the plan times the film with.

data.demo: the screenshots show demo data: rebuild their copy as it is
data.stand-in: the screenshots show real people's data: every name, email, phone number, address and case detail in the rebuilt UI is an invented stand-in, and the film says it is illustrative

rules: Full-screen UI: the app is rebuilt from its screenshots as live HTML (real text, crisp at 2× zoom, every control pressable) and fills the frame as its fit says; the screenshot itself is never shown as a picture.
Slow and clear beats short: camera moves take about 1 s, then the view holds 1.5 to 2 s before the next action; the cursor settles on a target before it clicks; when in doubt, slower.
Zoom in on what matters as it happens (about 1.4 to 2×), then pull back out; the camera never shows empty space past the UI's edges.
Only one thing moves while the viewer reads: no action starts while the step card is open, and the camera is still while text types.

Focus on the focus: whenever more than one object is in frame (a dialog over a page, two panels), everything that isn't the current subject sits under a soft scrim (about 50 %) and a light blur; when a second panel takes over, the first dims and blurs; everything comes back into focus at the hand-off.
Lively UI: cards rise with a slight overshoot, rows stagger in, buttons press and ripple, fields show a focus ring, spinners turn into checks, toasts slide in, dialogs scale in from where they open.
Nothing overset: every panel, card, menu, toast and pop-up stays fully inside the frame (and the aspect's safe area); check the right and bottom edges.
Readable at a glance: any text the viewer must read is large on screen after zooming (at least the stage's s size), on a solid surface.
The cursor is the brand's ink with a white edge and a soft shadow, large enough to follow on a phone; it never jumps, and while a view holds it idles with a slight drift, so nothing is ever frozen.
Each step's scene name is its title, so the film's timeline reads as chapters.
